text:
rachel: Quick sync: I prototyped a control-plane split where we advertise two distinct BGP/endpoint paths simultaneously and pick deterministically based on policy + probe health. Goal: let Dedicated customers route to a private endpoint for low latency but keep the peering path as a hot standby. Notes + questions below.

theo: high level sounds good. how are you planning to express preference in routing? BGP local-pref? community tags?

rachel: Thinking two-layer approach: prefer = local-pref bump on endpoint adverts + community tag for observability. If we need to force peering, withdraw the endpoint local-pref bump and/or prepend AS path on endpoint adverts. This avoids reprogramming tenant route tables.

samir: Important detail: some clouds (GCP) ignore local-pref from peer, so relying only on local-pref is brittle. We should implement a secondary signal: route-community + explicit agent preference flag so the tenant-side can prefer endpoint by policy locally.

lucy: Agreed. Also need clear healthcheck semantics. My proposal: endpoint considered healthy if: TCP established, TLS handshake success, application-level auth check (token introspect) succeeds. If any fails for >45s we start graceful failover.

rachel: Implementation sketch for probe + failover (agent or cp-driven):

```
probe: interval=10s timeout=5s
if (tcp && tls && auth) -> mark healthy
if (!healthy for 45s) -> mark endpoint_stale, announce peering-preferred policy
if (healthy for 120s) -> re-enable endpoint preference
```

samir: +1 but suggest jitter on probe start (0-2s) to avoid synchronized storms during region blips. Also add hysteresis window (120s as above) to avoid flapping.

theo: ops question: when both paths live, how do we steer egress NAT and preserve source IP? Some customers require srcip preservation to make ACLs work.

rachel: Two patterns: 1) Preserve-srcip via peering (no NAT) when traffic goes peering-first. 2) If endpoint path uses our regional relays and NAT, we clearly document _srcip_change_ in API and show per-tenant `srcip_mode`. We can offer NATed endpoint or direct VPC ENI attachment for zero-NAT (restricted).

lucy: We also need to think about TLS cert rotation timing: cert expiry + peering fallback can cascade. Ops playbook should recommend rotating certs in a rolling fashion and staggering peering maintenance windows.

ops-bot: automated note: current cert rotation cron runs 03:00 UTC, 30d before expiry. Any change requires runbook update: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/cert-rotation

samir: observability: expose metrics + traces: `attachment.active`, `attachment.health_seconds`, `attachment.switch_count`, `attachment.switch_reason{tls,tcp,auth,manual}`, and tag spans with `attachment_path=endpoint|peering` plus `attachment_id`.(alerts: >2 switches in 15m -> paged)

theo: API change suggestion: add `attachment_mode` to the tenant config with values: ["endpoint-prefer","peer-prefer","peer-only","endpoint-only"]. Keep it mutable and record `last_change_by` + audit log.

rachel: +1. For Private/on-prem customers default to `endpoint-only`. For Redwood-managed Dedicated default `endpoint-prefer`. We'll provide an override boolean `cp_controlled_routing=true|false` that controls whether the control plane can withdraw/adjust pref.

lucy: rollout plan: pilot internally -> 1st external pilot (low traffic customer) -> collect metrics 2w -> expand. Preflight script should check: BGP convergence time, no auth 5xx spikes, consistent srcip behavior.

samir: migration story for deprecating peering: create `deprecate_peering_ts` stamp; at T0 mark peering deprecated (UI + email), at T0+7d raise alerts for active connections on peering, at T0+30d withdraw peering adverts. Provide an escape hatch `force_peering_reinstate` with RBAC.

theo: security: make sure token scope is identical across both paths. If we rotate keys, ensure dual-signing or overlap window to avoid mass 401s. Also validate no privilege escalation when switching paths.

rachel: I'll draft RFC follow-up with: BGP policy examples, probe config, API fields, metrics list, runbook snippets and the pilot checklist. Assigning reviewers: @samir (observability), @lucy (ops), @theo (security). I'll post link here when done. :shipit:
